_doc: Purpose: drafting-standard profile for the ANSI/ASME (United States) system, consumed by cadcore.i18n.standards (projection angle plus sheet/line/lettering/title-block conventions). Background: standard-dependent values must live in data rather than code branches, and any field whose standard text was not obtained stays null and is listed in na_fields, so 'not fetched' can never masquerade as a real value; no standard text is reproduced here (R3).

source.retrieval_method: read-only fetch of public web pages and public PDFs (HTTP status recorded per URL); standard bodies are paywalled and none of their text is copied into this file

projection_angle_evidence.publisher: ASME (American Society of Mechanical Engineers), official standards catalogue page
projection_angle_evidence.shows: ASME Y14.3-2012 (R2024) 'Orthographic and Pictorial Views' is the current ASME standard for orthographic views on engineering drawing sheets; anchors the field to the US standard that governs view projection.
projection_angle_evidence.grade: official standards-developer page (scope text only, no clause text read)

projection_angle_evidence.publisher: Illinois State Board of Education (US state government agency), career and technical education curriculum
projection_angle_evidence.shows: Public US curriculum document stating that the United States adopted third-angle projection as its standard method on technical drawings (around 1890) while first-angle projection is primarily used in Europe and Asia (paraphrase; the document's wording is not copied here).

projection_angle_evidence.publisher: TU Darmstadt, Institute for Machine Elements and Machine Design (public German technical university tutorial)
projection_angle_evidence.shows: States that of the two projection methods in the ISO/DIN family, method 1 is usual in Germany and most European countries while method 3 is usually applied in the USA (paraphrase).

source.na_policy: null means not fetched (-1), never 'zero'; every null field is listed in na_fields, and no unverified field is given a guessed value.
notes: na_fields lists exactly the null-valued fields, in contract order: a gate can assert set(na_fields) == {k for k, v in profile.items() if v is None}.
ANSI/ASME sheet sizes (ASME Y14.1 series, inch based) are deliberately null: the values were not read, and they must not be conflated with ISO 216 A-series sizes.

projection_angle must differ from the GB/T profile so that the G2 drawing smoke can detect a standard switch actually changing the projection; this file carries third_angle while gbt.json carries first_angle.
